verdict_vs_market.quote: The offer is reasonable, but it isn't strong enough to justify leaving a job you're happy in.

verdict_vs_current.quote: Compared with your next 12 months at Meta: about +$76K, or +16%.

recommendation.quote: Negotiate. Don't accept as-is, and don't walk away yet.

equity_grounding.quote: Equity: You'd be giving up unvested Meta RSUs: $200K in the next 12 months, and probably more beyond that.

refresh_valued_at.quote: Most of the upside depends on refreshes that aren't guaranteed. You'd also be earning them as a new hire who hasn't been through a performance review cycle yet.

steady_state_math.quote: After Year 4, Google settles at about $532K/yr ($235K + $47K + $250K), roughly the same as Meta today.

uses_given_refresh_numbers.quote: If Google's refreshes come through as the recruiter described, 4-year comp is about $2.58M, or roughly $645K/yr on average.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: If they won't go above about $600K, staying at Meta is the better choice.

missing_info_requested: vesting schedule details (monthly vs quarterly, cliff)

ask_focus.quote: Push hardest on the new-hire RSUs, get the base above your current $240K, and add a sign-on.

year1_vs_recurring.quote: A realistic result would be about $250K base, $50K bonus, $1.25M in RSUs (about $312K/yr) and a $50K sign-on. That puts Year 1 around $660K

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: Sign-on: This covers the bonus you'd lose by leaving Meta before it pays out, plus the vesting you'd give up in the first year.
